note: The deck's guards on what it is handed and what it reports (NE-30j): the rate, a seek target, the duck, the duration, the reported rate, and the in-place seek's deadline. html-audio-backend.js asks these; AVDeck must answer the same. Port card NE-30s.

covers: html-audio-backend::a bad rate falls back to 1.0 rather than muting or reversing playback
cases.note: The rate a deck is handed: a positive number, else 1x — never muted, never reversed.

covers: html-audio-backend::seek moves the playhead and ignores junk
cases.note: A seek goes where it is told, and junk (negative, non-finite, not a number) is ignored: null means the deck does nothing.

covers: html-audio-backend::volume clamps to 0..1 — ducking uses this, not Web Audio
cases.note: The duck: clamped to 0..1, and junk is silence rather than a throw.

covers: html-audio-backend::duration is null rather than NaN when unknown
cases.note: What the deck reports as duration: finite, or null — never NaN.

covers: html-audio-backend::`rate` reports the element's real rate, so the lock screen cannot disagree with the audio
cases.note: The rate the lock screen extrapolates with is the one in force on the deck, not the one asked for.

covers: html-audio-backend::an in-place seek that never settles rejects rather than wedging the player
html-audio-backend::the deadline is read once per load, not re-read as visibility changes
cases.note: The in-place seek (same source) has a deadline, and it is the load's: one call per load or seek, answered from the visibility at that moment and kept for that load — a seek that never settles fails into the degrade path instead of wedging the player.

covers: html-audio-backend::the in-place seek path gets the same treatment
html-audio-backend::a hidden load that never settles still rejects
cases.note: Hidden, the same-source seek gets the hidden budget too: a refill waits on the same throttled queue a load does, and it still has a finite deadline.
A later slice EARLIER in the same episode is still a seek in the buffer the deck holds: the rule has no direction (deck/backwards-slices is the op log).
